item.title: Calculation of Stiefel fractions via Riemann thetas
item.description: arXiv:2611.17372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stiefel fraction is a deformation of Zolotarev one which allows to solve certain three band extentions of Zolotarev approximation problem. We propose an efficient computational approach for Stiefel's solution based on genus two Riemann theta functions. This allows us to visualise the domain in the space of three band problems corresponding to Stiefel's solutions.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Bogatyrev, Timur Garaev

item.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
item.description: arXiv:2611.17373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ with $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$, let $S(p)$ be the minimum of $|p(c)/(c\,p'(0))|$ over the critical points $c$ of $p$, and let $K(d)$ be the supremum of $S(p)$ over all such $p$ of degree $d$. In 1981 Smale proved that $K(d)\le 4$ for every $d$, and asked whether $4$ can be replaced by $1$. We prove that Smale's mean value constant $\sup_dK(d)$ equals $4$ and that $K(d)\to4$ as $d\to\infty$, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. In particular, $4$ cannot be replaced by any smaller constant. Each $K(d)$ is known to be below $4$, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_{\omega}$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_{\omega}$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.
item.dc:creator: J. Air\'an Santana-Rivero, Daniel Seco

item.title: On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.18185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Shuang-Shuang Yang, Dong-hai Zhao, Chung-Chun Yang, Liang-Wen Liao

item.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.
item.dc:creator: Muhan Luo, Marco Vergamini

item.title: Stable projective immersions of K\"ahler metrics with some radial symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.18016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We combine Calabi's criterion with Pringsheim's theorem to study projective inducibility under positive rescaling. By restricting to suitable radial holomorphic curves, we obtain an obstruction to local K\"ahler immersions into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space that applies uniformly to every positive rescaling. For invariant rational curves, we show that non-rationality of the moment map implies that no positive rescaling is projectively induced. We apply these criteria to the Taub-NUT, Candelas-de la Ossa, non-flat Stenzel, and Hwang-Singer scalar-flat metrics, as well as to Gibbons-Hawking metrics. Except for the Burns-Simanca metric in the Hwang-Singer family, no positive rescaling is projectively induced. For Gibbons-Hawking ALE spaces with at least two centres, the conclusion holds in every compatible complex structure. We also extend the results to complex space forms of arbitrary curvature with at least one finite signature index.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Arezzo, Andrea Loi, Giovanni Placini, Michela Zedda

item.title: Holomorphic one-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds of Kodaira codimension one
item.description: arXiv:2512.08395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a bimeromorphic classification of compact K\"ahler manifolds of Kodaira codimension one that admit a holomorphic one form without zeros.
item.dc:creator: Simon Pietig

item.title: Central Limit Theorems for Common Zeros via Bergman Kernels
item.description:
arXiv:2603.04588v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove central limit theorems as \(N	o\infty\) for common-zero statistics of \(k\) independent standard Gaussian holomorphic sections of \(L^N\), where \(L\) is a positive Hermitian holomorphic line bundle over a compact K"ahler manifold of complex dimension \(m\). For fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) forms \(\varphi\) of bidegree \((m-k,m-k)\) with \(\partial ar\partial\varphi
ot\equiv0\), we prove the CLT in codimensions \(2\leqslant k\leqslant m\) and show that the integrated coefficient in the Shiffman--Zelditch variance formula at scale \(N^{2k-m-2}\) is strictly positive. Shiffman and Zelditch proved the unconditioned smooth CLT for \(k=1\). For \(1\leqslant k\leqslant m\) we also prove a CLT for weighted volumes in fixed domains \(U\) with \(\mathscr C^2\) boundary and fixed real \(\mathscr C^3\) weights \(f\) whose restriction to \(\partial U\) is not identically zero. The variance of a weighted volume is asymptotic to \(N^{2k-m-1/2}
u_{m,k}\int_{\partial U}f^2\,\mathrm d\sigma\), with \(
u_{m,k}>0\) the Shiffman--Zelditch boundary constant and \(\sigma\) the induced surface measure. For \(k=m\) and \(f\equiv1\), the statistic counts common zeros in \(U\). Conditioning each section to vanish on the same fixed finite set preserves the leading variance and the Gaussian limit for both classes of tests, including smooth tests for \(k=1\). The set may meet \(\partial U\). A Bergman kernel criterion yields variance bounds and the new unconditioned CLTs from a uniform local \(L^2\) Bargmann--Fock limit and integrable off-diagonal derivative bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bin Guo

item.title: Boundary Behavior of Bisectional Curvatures for Weighted Bergman Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2605.17702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic boundary behavior of the holomorphic bisectional curvature for weighted Bergman metrics. By characterizing extremal functions via $L^2$-orthogonal projections, we establish an explicit formula for the weighted bisectional curvature. Utilizing the squeezing function, we then obtain quantitative upper and lower bounds for the curvature on bounded pseudoconvex domains. Furthermore, we prove that at strongly pseudoconvex boundary points, the bisectional curvature asymptotically coincides with that of the unit ball. As an application, these results provide a streamlined and unified proof for the known asymptotic behavior of the bisectional curvature of the K\"ahler-Einstein metric.
item.dc:creator: Sungmin Yoo

item.title: Transverse Analytic Envelopes and the Baum--Bott Rationality Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.05197v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study holomorphic first integrals near singular leaves through transverse analytic envelopes. For diagonal actions these are normal toric quotients, and complete semiglobal integrability along singular orbits with independent support weights is equivalent to maximal resonance rank and finite monodromy. For commuting fields in convergent simultaneous Poincar\'e--Dulac normal form, induced derivations determine the first-integral algebra. Labelled quotients and logarithmic residues reconstruct weights at maximal rank; Grassmannians describe the ambiguity otherwise. Polynomial examples show losses invisible to prescribed finite jets. For the Baum--Bott rationality conjecture, we prove rationality and an explicit residue formula for smooth compact singular components with product charts and a common invertible semisimple transverse linear part of maximal resonance rank. Equivariant cohomology gives higher-degree vanishing for affine diagonal torus actions, including intersecting singular strata.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: Resonant saddles, tangencies with small spheres, and the characteristic flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.14855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study resonant Siegel saddles in $\C^2$, with eigenvalue ratio $-p/q$, where $p,q$ are coprime positive integers, through their position relative to small round spheres. An intrinsic invariant $k$, defined through a resonance index that measures approximate first integrals, equals the first resonant obstruction. For $k<\infty$, the maximal contact order with the linear foliation is $m=k(p+q)+1$, and suitably normalized charts give $2k$ tangency circles. We compute their transverse type: resonant terms cancel to first order, and Poincar\'e--Dulac normalization through degree $2m-1$ makes every contact a saddle, while weaker normalization can produce elliptic arcs and periodic characteristic orbits. For the exact model we describe the whole-sphere flow and the correspondence between its tangency circles and separatrix sectors. In arbitrary charts the characteristic return map near a separatrix circle realizes its holonomy, whose $p$-th iterate has, when $k<\infty$, multiplicity $kp+1$, with $kp$ attracting and $kp$ repelling petals. Classical rigidity of resonant holonomy then recovers the analytic saddle class from $C^1$ orbital equivalence near that circle. We also describe tangency loci for arbitrary nondegenerate germs by the numerical range and the leading orbital form.
item.dc:creator: Toshikazu Ito \and Bruno Sc\'ardua

item.title: A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
item.description: arXiv:2610.17876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article investigates random Dirichlet series within the framework of Hardy and mixed norm spaces of Dirichlet series. For randomization methods by sequences of non-constant independent and identically distributed random variables, we completely characterize when the random symbol space of the Hardy space $\mathscr{H}^p$ (respectively, the mixed norm space $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_{\alpha}$) coincides with $\mathscr{H}^2$ (respectively, $\mathscr{H}^{2,q}_{\alpha}$). We also obtain some integrability results when Dirichlet series belong to the corresponding random symbol spaces. The same methods also yield a complete characterization for mixed norm spaces on the unit disk in the range $0<q<4$, closing the gap between previously known necessary and sufficient conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jiale Chen, Min He, Maofa Wang

item.title: On intersections of function fields
item.description: arXiv:2603.29609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{R}$ and $Y:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{T}$ be holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces such that $X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cdot Y^*M(\mathcal{T})=M(\mathcal{E})$, where $M(\mathcal{S})$ denotes the field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}$. We study the problem of determining when the degree $[M(\mathcal{E}):X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cap Y^*M(\mathcal{T})]$ is finite and attains the minimal possible value $\mathrm{deg}\,X\cdot\mathrm{deg}\,Y$. When $X$ is a Galois covering, we give a complete characterization in terms of factorizations of $Y$ into an equivariant map followed by a Galois covering. We also establish some results without the maximality condition, as well as general results on the functional equation $A\circ X=B\circ Y$ when one of the maps involved is a Galois covering.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Pakovich
